metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >45.0), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly; reduce forecast by 5–10% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility and overconfidence; dampen forecast variance and anchor to recent 7-day moving average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 14-day average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline (e.g., drop >5% from day 1), model often fails to anticipate; adjust forecast downward by 3–8% for first 3 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overfit recent highs; use 14-day rolling average as baseline for smoothing, especially when sentiment is neutral.
